name_reason: Fully compliant with the global naming convention: data_fd2_ prefix + battle_ core-table marker + descriptor character_base_table; the _table suffix reflects the array datatype. No Ghidra address residue in the name. The implied dimensions (32 entries, 24-byte stride) are semantic domain values (32 playable characters, sizeof(character_base)=24), not address artifacts.
purpose: Read-only player-character base/debut stat table: one fixed-layout entry per playable character id (char_id 0..0x1F = 32 entries), supplying starting race/class/level and base HP/MP/MV/AP/DP/DX plus the initial spell and item loadout.
logic_summary: Const array of 32 x struct character_base (24-byte stride). Indexed only through accessor fd2_get_char_base_entry @ 0x4E4E8 (returns base + idx*0x18 = &entry.race_id). The two readers fd2_init_runtime_char_for_battle (0x10C50) and fd2_init_runtime_char_from_base_growth (0x112A5) combine these base values with the per-portrait character_growth table to populate a runtime_char slot: HP=base.hp+(level-1)*growth.hp_min and MP likewise (level-1 factor), while AP=base.ap+level*growth.ap_min and DP/DX likewise (level factor). base.race_id/class_id are copied to runtime_char +0x1F/+0x20; the initial_spells[4] block is memmove'd to the spell bitmap and initial_items[6] seed the inventory slots (0xFF=empty). Verified byte-exact against FD2.LE memory at 0x61DA1 (e.g. entry 0x07 HP=0x0119=281).
datatype: const character_base[32]  (768 bytes; element = struct character_base, 24 bytes, pack(1), little-endian)
element_semantics: struct character_base per entry: race_id(+0,u8), class_id(+1,u8), level(+2,u8 starting level), hp(+3,u16 base HP), mp(+5,u16 base MP), mv(+7,u8 movement), initial_spells[4](+8,u8 spell ids, 0=none), initial_items[6](+0xC,u8 item ids, 0xFF=empty slot), ap(+0x12,u16 base attack), dp(+0x14,u16 base defense), dx(+0x16,u16 base evasion/agility). Index = char_id in [0,0x1F].
notes: Single DATA xref to the table address is the accessor fd2_get_char_base_entry (0x4E4E8); both downstream readers go through that accessor, and game-side write-xrefs are zero -> const confirmed. src comment block at btltab3.c lines 744-758 was already a precise final-conclusion description (struct layout, accessor, readers, const status, stat formulas) and is byte-exact-correct against memory, so comment_verdict=keep and btltab3.c was NOT edited (only the shard is staged for the src side). The data-address plate at 0x61DA1 was previously null; created a concise plate (753 chars) summarizing the src conclusion via cu.setComment(PLATE_COMMENT,...). struct character_base typedef confirmed in src/include/types.h lines 113-125. fd2-knowledge skill corroborates 24-byte char_base_entry = '人物出場屬性' (character debut/base attributes).
